text: # Addendum 029-A: Seldon never reads a relationship by name alone
### R3. Hermes Agent install (runtime without binary on PATH)
### R4. Wintermute MCP server — not registered

- R1: block = within-workout grouping (canonical word = physical name; superset/
  circuit/complex/EMOM/Tabata = `block_type` polymorphic subtypes).

- R2: `:Cycle` base type + `cycle_type` enum (macro/meso/micro); full relabel of the
  4 `:Block` nodes; `block_id`→`cycle_id`; cycle MCP tools; seed-all-three-from-real-
  anchors (1 macro, 4 meso, micros-from-weeks).

R1 **Nothing is required beyond what a set is.** A set = exercise + whatever of
reps / load / duration actually happened. Everything else (session effort, workout
duration, notes, equipment, treatments, failed, pain_scale, rest) is present only
if given. No defaults, no placeholders, no prompts, no `required` attributes, no
validation that rejects a submission for a missing optional field, no display
that calls out absence. Absence is data.

R2 **Per-set RPE is gone from planning too.** The 08-16 ruling removed it from the
logger. pb-03/pb-04 (Desktop spec error) reintroduced `rpe` in the compressed JSON
contract and a gear-popover field in the builder. Remove both.
`PlannedSet.prescribed_rpe` stays as a column (history), is never written by the
GUI, and is not rendered.

R1 **`exercise_id` is the identity. `exercise_name` in `sets` is the as-logged
label and is never a grouping key, join key, or filter key on any read surface.**
Display name comes from the Exercise node (`name`) via id.

R2 **Writers store the canonical display name.** `log_workout`, `amend_workout`,
the logger form, `mirror_plan_to_postgres`: after resolution, `exercise_name` :=
the Exercise node's `name`. The string the user typed is kept, if it differs, in
`sets.extra.logged_as` (jsonb), so the alias evidence is not lost. No backfill
rewrite of historical `exercise_name` (history stays as logged; R1 makes it
harmless).

R3 **Mis-resolved sets are corrected by `amend_workout`, never by UPDATE.** Each
correction is one effect-verified amend with the reason in the amend note.
